_status: DRAFT, NOT IMPORTED. Mali researched as part of a push into WAEMU/Sahel territory the branch's source docx had only described in undifferentiated bloc-level prose without naming individual countries. Mali is notable as AFRISTAT's headquarters and as a country whose statistics have operated under real political strain (2012 crisis, 2020/2021 coups, ECOWAS sanctions period) -- researched directly rather than assuming either a functioning or a collapsed system. Sitting in src/data/research/ pending Thomas's review.
_note: AFRISTAT's own site states plainly it is headquartered in Bamako, Mali, and independently documents leading the WAEMU-wide IHPC renovation project with INSTAT Mali's own Director General chairing a November 2024 Bamako workshop validating the draft base-2023 regulation (also attended by AFRISTAT, BCEAO and IMF staff) -- the strongest institutional AFRISTAT-country linkage found anywhere in this branch. AFRISTAT itself is still not minted as a node (an institution without a titled publication, per this corpus's own rule), but a UEMOA Commission document describing the WAEMU-wide harmonised CPI framework -- including a named, numbered regulation (Reglement N 03/2017/CM/UEMOA) -- was independently opened and quoted, giving this branch its first genuinely-researched bloc-level document. It describes the base-2014 generation of the WAEMU harmonised CPI; Mali's own INSTAT page shows the country has since rebased to base 2023, and the Bamako workshop confirms a base-2023 successor regulation was still in draft, not yet Council-of-Ministers-adopted, as of November 2024 -- so the edge below is recorded as a citation to the WAEMU framework generally, not a current-methodology dependency, and flagged accordingly. On social protection, Mali's flagship cash-transfer programme (Jigisemejiri) is the most concrete finding: two independent World Bank documents show a flat monthly amount increased once, in 2018, explicitly 'on account of inflation and currency devaluation' but with no formula -- and the programme itself formally closed 30 June 2023, with no confirmed successor located.

_open_questions.question: If AFRISTAT (or a specific titled AFRISTAT publication, e.g. the numbered newsletter 'La Lettre d'AFRISTAT') is ever minted as a node, should country be 'ML' (AFRISTAT's own text: "AFRISTAT, qui a son siege a Bamako au Mali") or 'INT' (AFRISTAT's own text also self-describes as an international organisation founded by treaty among 14 African Franc Zone states)? Both are documented and defensible; not resolved this session.

A November 2024 Bamako workshop (opened by INSTAT Mali's own Director General) validated a draft UEMOA regulation adopting the base-2023 IHPC, ahead of submission to the Council of Ministers -- no later document confirming formal Council-of-Ministers adoption was found, even though Mali's own INSTAT page already publishes on base 2023 today. Sequencing between national implementation and Union-wide legal adoption is unresolved.

Mali's Jigisemejiri cash-transfer programme formally closed 30 June 2023 per its own World Bank technical paper. A November 2022 news article discussed a planned 'deuxieme generation' from 2023, but no document confirming what (if anything) replaced Jigisemejiri as of 2026 was located.

Mali's 2025 Article IV Consultation report references 'Annex VIII. Data Issues' (p.50), which very likely contains a formal SDDS/GDDS characterization and CPI-specific commentary, but the annex itself could not be retrieved this session (blocked by an Akamai edge response on direct download; WebFetch returned only the table-of-contents reference).

reports.title: Indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation (IHPC)
reports.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique du Mali (INSTAT)
reports.description: Mali's harmonised consumer price index, base 2023 (replacing base 2014, itself replacing base 2008 and the original 1996 rollout). "Cet indice est harmonise car la methodologie utilisee pour sa production est identique dans les huit pays membres de l'Union Economique et Monetaire Ouest Africaine (UEMOA)." Formula changed at the 2023 rebasing from Laspeyres to a chained Young index ("un indice de Young chaine"); basket now 766 varieties across 4,927 points of sale, roughly 30,150 monthly price observations, versus ~650 varieties and 3,344 outlets under the outgoing base-2014 methodology.
reports.cadence_note: Monthly bulletin archive on INSTAT's own site runs unbroken (all twelve months listed per year) from 2009 through 2025, plus January-June 2026 as of this session's check -- including full coverage through the 2012 crisis year and both 2020/2021 coup years.

release_schedule.note: No dated release calendar or stated publication rule found for IHPC specifically (the site's only 'Calendrier de diffusion' PDF is a general SSN calendar dated 2021). Instead, the monthly bulletin PDFs' own embedded CreationDate metadata was checked directly for the six most recent 2026 releases, giving the publication lag after each reference month: Jan-2026 data -> published 2026-02-12 (ihpc0126_pub.pdf); Feb-2026 -> 2026-03-11; Mar-2026 -> 2026-04-10; Apr-2026 -> 2026-05-19; May-2026 -> 2026-06-10; Jun-2026 -> 2026-07-10 (ihpc0626_pub.pdf, the latest posted as of this check). This is a consistent ~day-10-to-19-of-next-month pattern. As of 2026-08-11, no July-2026 bulletin (ihpc0726_pub.pdf, checked directly, returns 404) or press release page has appeared yet, so the next release is projected in the 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-19 window by this observed lag, not a published date.

reports.title: Enquête Harmonisée sur les Conditions de Vie des Ménages (EHCVM) 2021
reports.publisher: Institut National de la Statistique du Mali (INSTAT)
reports.description: Household living-conditions survey supplying the expenditure weights for the base-2023 IHPC: "les ponderations proviennent de l'enquete harmonisee sur les conditions de vie des menages « EHCVM 2021 »." Part of the same WAEMU-wide harmonised EHCVM round fielded in Senegal and Côte d'Ivoire for their own 2021-2022 CPI rebasings.

reports.title: Indice Harmonisé des Prix à la Consommation (IHPC) au sein de l'UEMOA
reports.region: WAEMU (8 member states, incl. Mali, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal)
reports.description: The UEMOA Commission's own descriptive note on the Union-wide Harmonised CPI (dated avril 2023, published mai 2023), describing the then-current base-2014 generation: "Ce dernier indice a ete valide par le reglement N 03/2017/CM/UEMOA portant adoption des modalites d'elaboration et de calcul de l'Indice Harmonise des Prix a la Consommation au sein des Etats membres de l'UEMOA (IHPC base 100 en 2014)." States the index is Laspeyres-type, weights from national consumption/poverty surveys fielded 2011-2014, classified under NCOA-IHPC (a WAEMU-specific nomenclature "derivee de la COICOP"). Independently opened and quoted by two separate country-level research passes this session (Mali and Côte d'Ivoire) -- this branch's first bloc-level WAEMU/UEMOA document to be directly researched rather than only referenced in secondary summaries. Describes the base-2014 generation; both Mali and Côte d'Ivoire have since rebased nationally to base 2023, and a successor Union-wide regulation was still in draft, not confirmed adopted, as of a November 2024 validation workshop.

dependencies.basis: INSTAT Mali's own IHPC methodology page: "...les ponderations proviennent de l'enquete harmonisee sur les conditions de vie des menages « EHCVM 2021 »".

WEAK/COMPOSITE EVIDENCE, kept and flagged rather than dropped, per this branch's own precedent for low-confidence-but-real findings (see au-cgc-gst-relativities). No single document states this Mali-specific link directly: INSTAT Mali's own page states its methodology "est identique dans les huit pays membres de l'UEMOA," and this UEMOA note separately states the Union-wide IHPC (of which Mali is one of the eight producing states by treaty membership) "a ete valide par le reglement N 03/2017/CM/UEMOA." The regulation this note describes covers the base-2014 generation; Mali's live IHPC is now base 2023, and the base-2023 successor regulation was still in draft as of November 2024 (see ml-uemoa-base2023-regulation-adoption-unconfirmed). Downgraded from methodology_depends_on to cites to reflect both the compositional and generational gaps.

_dropped.why: AFRISTAT is confirmed headquartered in Bamako, Mali ("AFRISTAT, qui a son siege a Bamako au Mali...") and is repeatedly documented leading/supporting the IHPC renovation project across WAEMU member states, twice pinned specifically to Bamako workshops with INSTAT Mali's own Director General presiding (Nov 2021 training workshop; Nov 2024 base-2023 validation workshop, also attended by BCEAO and IMF staff). AFRISTAT itself is an institution without a titled publication and fails this corpus's node rule. See ml-afristat-node-country-judgment-call for the country-code question if a future session mints it.

Two independent World Bank documents describe Mali's flagship cash-transfer safety net (Jigisemejiri) paying a fixed monthly amount (FCFA 10,000, later FCFA 15,000) with no stated indexation formula. The one documented increase (2018) is explicitly attributed to 'inflation and currency devaluation' as a rationale -- "The resources allowed for an increase in both the number of transfer beneficiaries as well as the transfer amount, on account of inflation and currency devaluation" -- but is a one-off, refinancing-linked adjustment, not a rule. No node minted for Jigisemejiri itself (a programme, not a titled recurring publication); the programme formally closed 30 June 2023 with no confirmed successor (see ml-jigisemejiri-successor-unconfirmed).

_dropped.edge: INPS pension (Institut National de Prevoyance Sociale) -> ml-instat-ihpc
_dropped.why: A one-time initial-pension calculation formula was found via CLEISS (a secondary, French government liaison source): 26% of average monthly salary over the last 8 contributory years, plus 2% per 12-month contribution period, up to 120 months. No post-retirement indexation/adjustment mechanism to CPI or any other index is stated anywhere in that source. Primary INPS legal text (Loi n96-004 du 26 janvier 1996) not retrieved this session.
